title.narrative: Scaling up Child Protection Interventions for Vulnerable Children and Caregivers in Monguno LGA, Borno State

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtIn Monguno, GPON’s assessments and sector data indicate that approximately 25% of vulnerable children are unaccompanied or separated, 20% are at risk of or subjected to child marriage, and up to 40% suffer psychosocial distress requiring structured PSS support. Furthermore, at least 15% are children with disabilities, who remain disproportionately excluded from services. These figures highlight the scale and diversity of protection risks facing children, underscoring the need for a comprehensive, multisectoral response.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe humanitarian crisis in northeast Nigeria remains critical, with conflict, displacement, and food insecurity converging to heighten risks for children. The 2025 HRP identifies 7.8 million people in need across the BAY states, including 1.9 million children requiring urgent child protection services. The 2025 HNO highlights widespread family separation, child marriage, child labor, psychosocial distress, and exclusion of children with disabilities as urgent protection concerns.ltbrgtThe 2025 Lean Season Plan projects 31 million Nigerians acutely food insecure, including 4.6 million in BAY states. In Borno alone, 300,000 children are projected to suffer from SAM, with up to 150 nutrition facilities at risk of closure due to funding shortfalls. Food insecurity directly increases child protection risks, as families adopt harmful coping strategies such as child labor, early marriage, or relinquishing children into unsafe arrangements.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtMonguno LGA, on the northern Borno frontline, is among the most affected. It hosts large numbers of IDPs and returnees, where overstretched services and weak protection systems leave children exposed. GPON’s assessments show:lt/pgtltpgtltbrgt1. UASC remain largely unsupported due to insufficient family tracing and reunification (FTR) capacity.ltbrgt2. Child marriage and labor are rising as households face extreme economic pressures.ltbrgt3. Children suffer psychosocial distress without access to safe spaces or structured PSS.ltbrgt4. Children with disabilities face systemic exclusion and neglect.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtGPON is currently implementing an NHF-supported 1st Standard Allocation child protection project in Monguno, covering just 5% of identified child protection needs, leaving a 95% gap. This new NHF-funded project will scale up lifesaving child protection services to address this gap. Activities include case management, FTR, psychosocial support, positive parenting and adolescent life skills, disability-inclusive services, and strengthening of CBCPMs. It will also deliver community awareness on child protection, PSEA, and referral pathways, ensuring integration with nutrition, WASH, and health sectors.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe project’s overall objective is to safeguard and strengthen the protection environment for children and caregivers in Monguno during the lean season. It will directly target 4545 individuals (2537 children 2,008 caregivers), including at least 1,500 persons with disabilities, and indirectly benefit 25,000 community members.ltbrgtAligned with the NHF Lean Season Allocation Strategy Paper, the project prioritizes UASC, adolescent girls, children with disabilities, and other high-risk groups. It also mainstreams gender, AAP, PSEA, and disability inclusion, while leveraging GPON’s presence and local staff for rapid, cost-effective, and sustainable delivery.ltbrgtlt/pgt
